title: Kapoor Singh in Malwa and Ala Singh’s Entry into the Khalsa

blocks.text: During the upheavals caused by repeated invasions, the Khalsa is forced to keep moving, and Kapoor Singh leads his contingent into the Malwa country among the Brars. The page emphasizes insecurity, shortage, and mobility, showing how survival depends upon constant movement rather than settled control.

Even in that uncertainty, local bonds matter. Men such as Gohar Singh and Gurbakhsh Singh sustain the Singhs with food, shelter, and political goodwill, demonstrating that service to the Panth could reshape regional power just as surely as battlefield prowess.

Ala Singh rises within this world of alliance and provision. By feeding the Khalsa, associating himself with its leadership, and accepting initiation, Ala Singh joined the fraternity of the Khalsa Panth, turning practical support into a more durable religious and political bond.
